headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because Khoj reads indexed notes/files and can use broad network egress, while the other agent is an unverified prompt-engineering content source with no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a content-writing repository with no runtime isolation, while B ingests indexed documents and notes by default. If A’s content is copied into B’s retrieval corpus or prompts, B may treat attacker-controlled text as instruction-like content. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented for this pair, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is added to agent_b's indexed notes or prompt corpus
IF agent_b treats retrieved text as instruction-bearing content without provenance checks
mitigations: Restrict agent_b indexing to trusted folders only
Add a provenance banner to retrieved snippets
Disable automatic execution of retrieved instructions
Review any agent_a-derived prompt templates before ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly reads indexed personal notes/files and handles model-provider API keys, while A is an unverified open-source content-writing repo with no stated data controls. If A is used to generate or transform content that enters B’s indexed workspace, sensitive notes can be exposed through retrieval or downstream outputs. The pairwise leakage path is inferred, not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_a-produced text is stored in agent_b's indexed files
IF agent_b is configured to sync or search sensitive personal notes
mitigations: Keep sensitive notes out of shared indexes
Separate API-key material from indexed content
Limit agent_b to a dedicated non-sensitive workspace
Rotate any exposed model-provider keys
requires-engineering: add per-document access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no declared write or network capabilities, while B cannot write the filesystem or modify git state and only has read access plus broad egress. There is little direct write-write overlap, so conflict risk is limited. Because A’s runtime capabilities are unverified and empty fields are informative, I avoid assuming more overlap than shown.
conditions: IF agent_a is wrapped in an external orchestrator that adds write access
IF both agents are granted the same mutable external resource outside these profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents on separate workspaces
Do not grant shared git credentials
Avoid mounting the same writable directory
Document any added external write scopes

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s retrieval/chat workflow can consume text from indexed documents, and A is a content-writing source that may emit persuasive but unverified material. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into summaries or actions. The pair lacks direct verification or provenance controls in the profiles, so medium is warranted rather than low.
conditions: IF agent_a output is inserted into agent_b's knowledge base
IF agent_b uses retrieved text without a verification step
mitigations: Require citation checks before reuse
Mark agent_a output as untrusted draft text
Add a human review step for downstream actions
Separate generated content from source notes

E_compliance.rationale: B touches personal notes and indexed documents and may use cloud or self-hosted servers plus configured search providers, while A is an open-source content-writing repo with no compliance controls stated. If personal or regulated notes flow through B and are influenced by A-generated content, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The mismatch is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated personal notes are indexed by agent_b
IF agent_b routes queries to external search providers or cloud services
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from external search
Confirm residency settings for agent_b deployments
Document retention periods for indexed notes
Add deletion/export procedures for indexed content
